name: Guiding Principles
purpose: A visual aid to highlight a mind-set for healthy dialogues to make better business decisions.
whereUsed: The Guiding Principles are best used in the Problem Space during the Awareness and Analysis Phases to confirm the expected mind-set required for healthy dialogues and better decision-making. They are also useful in the Solution Space to serve as a reminder of the mind-set required to ensure the productive use of resources to get the best possible results (outcomes).
why: We will create a more collaborative environment to ensure the best use of our collective time and resources.
outcomes: A more comfortable and resourceful atmosphere

spaces.heading: IF WE ARE IN THE “PROBLEM SPACE” WE NEED TO:
steps: Acknowledge the lack of guiding principles contribute to wasting time, people (talent), resources, and capital
Confirm how the guiding principles will enable better dialogues to make better business decisions with less waste
Introduce the guiding principles as an integrated part of the KA DecisionMaking Standards (Mind-set, Skill-set, Tool-set)
Agree to continuously reference and apply the guiding principles (Mind-Set)

spaces.heading: IF WE ARE IN THE “SOLUTION SPACE” WE NEED TO:
steps: Confirm how business decisions have been made to date (completeness, consensus, confidence)
Challenge how “business as usual/ expected” can be dramatically improved through the use of the guiding principles (Mind-set)
Agree to start using the guiding principles as an integrated part of the KA Decision-Making Standards (Mind-set, Skill-set, Tool-set)
